newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Thousands of Jews assemble to show claim to Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Jews assemble to show claim to Hebron.

text.p: Thousands of religious Jews made a pilgrimage to Hebron on Friday for the annual reading of a biblical passage showing what they regard as their birthright to the occupied West Bank town.
"Hebron is for Hebrew people," read one protest sign reflecting opposition to any handover of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.

Dozens of buses brought observant Jews to join the 400-strong settler community for the annual reading of the biblical tale of patriarch Abraham's purchase of a burial area in Hebron for his wife Sarah.
The Tomb of the Patriarchs in Hebron, traditionally the site bought by Abraham, is now a complex revered by both Jews and Moslems. It is known to Moslems as the al-Ibrahimi mosque.
In February 1994 a Jewish militant from Kiryat Arba settlement adjacent to Hebron shot dead 29 Moslems at prayer in the mosque. He was beaten to death by survivors.
Israel and the PLO are currently locked in U.S.-brokered negotiations on implementing a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment from most of the town of 100,000 Palestinians.

Right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeks to modify the Hebron deal signed by the previous Labour-led government to give extra protection to the militant settlers who live in the heart of the city. Palestinians reject any changes to the accord.
"It will be a holocaust for all the Jewish people," Benny Shmuel, from the central Israeli town of Ramat Ban, said in Hebron about an Israeli pullback.

Israel's Channel One Television said it had obtained a classified report by police and the secret service warning that security should be tightened around Netanyahu once a pullback begins in case of an attack by ultranationalist Jews.
A religious Jew opposed to peace deals with the Palestinians assassinated Labour Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin last November.
A militant Jewish leader of the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement who lives in Hebron said on Friday Netanyahu had no right to hand the West Bank town to Palestinian rule.

"At least half the state voted for Netanyahu in order that he would stop Hebron, the process in Hebron...Netanyahu has no right to implement the withdrawal in Hebron," Baruch Merzel told Israel Radio.
Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak confirmed Israeli officials met on Thursday night to discuss how to deal with Jewish militants who might actively oppose agreement to leave most of Hebron.
Channel One asked Bazak how Netanyahu could take a "strong hand" against even a part of the right-wing public that had voted him into office.

"A strong hand is not directed against the right or the left, against this or that man," Bazak said. "A strong hand, when necessary, is to be directed against someone who breaks the law and it is not connected to his political identification."
Israel's Haaretz newspaper said the meeting focused on issuing administrative detention orders which would allow security forces to imprison Jewish militants without trial.
Israel Television and radio early on Friday said such an order had already been issued against Merzel but the Israeli army denied the reports.
